walkthroughs.body_html:
Biodiversity & Natural Resources — a core area of A-Level Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Biodiversity & Natural Resources brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Biodiversity & Natural Resources.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Higher Simpson's diversity index D indicates:
options: Lower biodiversity
Higher biodiversity
No biodiversity
Same biodiversity

mcqs.q: Captive breeding is an example of:
options: In situ conservation
Ex situ conservation
Reforestation
Succession

mcqs.q: How does a population of organisms become better adapted to its environment over time?
options: Individual organisms change during their lifetime in response to their environment and pass the changes on to offspring.
Organisms decide what features they need and grow them by force of will.
Individuals with advantageous heritable variations survive and reproduce more; their alleles increase in frequency over generations.
ADH directly opens holes in the collecting duct that let urine escape.

mcqs.q: What actually changes during natural selection in a population?
options: The frequencies of alleles in the population's gene pool change across generations.
Organisms decide what features they need and grow them by force of will.
Individual organisms change their own genes to adapt.
The entire DNA sequence of every individual changes simultaneously.

mcqs.q: How does ADH affect the collecting duct in the kidney?
options: ADH actively pumps water out of urine into the blood.
It increases the permeability of the collecting duct to water (by inserting aquaporins), so more water is reabsorbed and urine is more concentrated.
ADH directly opens holes in the collecting duct that let urine escape.
The entire DNA sequence of every individual changes simultaneously.
